name: Hydrogen
note: Most abundant element in the universe; fuses to light every star; one proton, one electron — the simplest gate.

name: Helium
note: Second-most abundant in the cosmos; utterly inert; becomes a frictionless superfluid near absolute zero.

name: Lithium
note: Lightest metal — floats on water; runs every rechargeable battery and steadies the bipolar mind.

name: Beryllium
note: Light, rigid, transparent to X-rays; windows for radiation optics; its dust is poison.

name: Boron
note: Borosilicate glass and the neutron-drinking control rod; hard, high-melting metalloid.

name: Carbon
note: The backbone of all life; one atom, many faces — graphite, diamond, graphene, the buckyball.

name: Nitrogen
note: 78% of the air; inert as gas, violent as nitrate; the fertilizer that feeds the world.

name: Oxygen
note: What we breathe; rusts iron and feeds fire — and David's gate where it lands square: 1:1, the balanced state.

name: Fluorine
note: The most reactive, most electronegative element; attacks nearly everything; gives us Teflon and toothpaste.

name: Neon
note: Inert noble gas; glows orange-red in a tube — the light of the sign and the city night.

name: Sodium
note: Symbol Na, from natrium; soft enough to cut, explosive in water; half of salt and the spark of every nerve.

name: Magnesium
note: Burns blinding white; the light structural metal; the green heart of chlorophyll.

name: Aluminium
note: Most abundant metal in the crust; light, strong, endlessly recyclable — once dearer than gold.

name: Silicon
note: Sand, glass, and the thinking chip; second-most abundant in the crust — the substrate of the digital age.

name: Phosphorus
note: Glows in the dark; the P in DNA and ATP; gives both the match and the nerve agent.

name: Sulfur
note: Brimstone; rotten eggs and struck matches; its acid runs all of industry.

name: Chlorine
note: Green choking gas; disinfects water and bleaches cloth — and was the first chemical weapon.

name: Argon
note: The lazy gas; fills bulbs and shields welds; third-most abundant in the air.

name: Potassium
note: Symbol K, from kalium; softer and more violent than sodium; the other half of the nerve impulse.

name: Calcium
note: Bone, shell, and chalk; the reactive metal that builds every skeleton.

name: Scandium
note: Rare and light; aluminium-scandium alloys for aerospace frames and fighter jets.

name: Titanium
note: Strong as steel at half the weight, and it never rusts; jet engines, hip implants, white paint.

name: Vanadium
note: Toughens steel; the redox-flow battery; a chemist's rainbow of oxidation colors.

name: Chromium
note: The shine of chrome; turns steel stainless; the green of emerald and the red of ruby.

name: Manganese
note: Makes steel tough and bright; the black of the dry-cell battery; an essential trace nutrient.

name: Iron
note: Symbol Fe, from ferrum; the core of the Earth and of your blood; where stellar fusion ends and civilization began.

name: Cobalt
note: The deep blue of glass and glaze; the lithium cathode; the metal at the center of vitamin B12.

name: Nickel
note: Coins and stainless steel; magnetic; with iron it makes the planet's molten core.

name: Copper
note: Symbol Cu, from cuprum; the first metal humans worked; the wire that carries the current; the green of Liberty.

name: Zinc
note: Galvanizes steel against rust; brass with copper; the trace metal your immune system needs.

name: Gallium
note: Melts in the warmth of your hand; the semiconductor of the LED and the fast radio chip.

name: Germanium
note: The metalloid of the first transistor; now fiber-optic cores and infrared lenses.

name: Arsenic
note: The classic poison of kings; also the dopant that tunes a semiconductor.

name: Selenium
note: The photoconductor of the first photocopier; an essential trace element, toxic in excess.

name: Bromine
note: One of only two liquid elements; red and choking; flame retardants and old photographic film.

name: Krypton
note: Noble gas that once defined the metre by its light; high-performance lamps and lasers.

name: Rubidium
note: Soft and violently reactive; the heartbeat of one kind of atomic clock.

name: Strontium
note: The blazing red of fireworks and emergency flares; its isotope seeks bone.

name: Yttrium
note: High-temperature superconductors; the red phosphor of the old picture tube; white LEDs.

name: Zirconium
note: Corrosion-proof; the cladding around nuclear fuel; cubic zirconia counterfeits the diamond.

name: Niobium
note: The superconducting magnet of the MRI and the particle accelerator; micro-alloyed pipeline steel.

name: Molybdenum
note: High-melting; toughens steel; the metal at the heart of nitrogen-fixing enzymes.

name: Technetium
note: The first element made by humans; no stable isotope exists; the workhorse tracer of medical imaging.

name: Ruthenium
note: Hardens platinum; a catalyst and a data-storage layer; one of the platinum-group rarities.

name: Rhodium
note: The most reflective metal; the catalytic converter's prize; rarer and dearer than gold.

name: Palladium
note: Drinks hydrogen like a sponge; the catalytic converter; the metal of cold-fusion lore.

name: Silver
note: Symbol Ag, from argentum; the best electrical conductor of all; mirrors, coins, the metal of the moon.

name: Cadmium
note: Toxic; the cadmium red and yellow of the painter; the rechargeable NiCd cell.

name: Indium
note: Soft as wax; the transparent conductor (ITO) printed on every touchscreen.

name: Tin
note: Symbol Sn, from stannum; bronze with copper, solder for circuits; bends with a 'cry'; the humble can.

name: Antimony
note: Symbol Sb, from stibium; the ancient kohl of the eye; flame retardants; it hardens lead.

name: Tellurium
note: The metalloid of thin-film solar cells; it leaves a rare-earth garlic on the breath.

name: Iodine
note: Purple vapor; the antiseptic and the thyroid's element; why salt is iodized.

name: Xenon
note: Noble gas of the bright headlight and the ion thruster; a gas that can put you to sleep.

name: Caesium
note: The most reactive metal; the second itself is defined by the vibration of its atom.

name: Barium
note: The white of the X-ray 'barium meal'; the green of fireworks; the weight in drilling mud.

name: Lanthanum
note: First of the lanthanides; camera-lens glass and the nickel-metal-hydride battery.

name: Cerium
note: Most abundant rare earth; the lighter flint, the glass polish, the catalytic converter.

name: Praseodymium
note: The green of rare-earth glass; powerful magnets; the welder's protective goggles.

name: Neodymium
note: The strongest permanent magnet — in every hard drive, earbud, and wind turbine.

name: Promethium
note: Radioactive with no stable isotope; the glow of luminous paint and the atomic battery.

name: Samarium
note: Samarium-cobalt magnets that keep their strength in fierce heat.

name: Europium
note: The red and blue phosphor of the screen; the secret ink in a euro banknote.

name: Gadolinium
note: The MRI contrast agent; near room temperature its magnetism runs to extremes.

name: Terbium
note: Green phosphors and alloys that change shape inside a magnetic field.

name: Dysprosium
note: Keeps a hot magnet from forgetting itself; a neutron-eater in control rods.

name: Holmium
note: The strongest magnetic moment of any element; the surgeon's cutting laser.

name: Erbium
note: Amplifies the light inside a fiber-optic cable; the pink of glass and laser.

name: Thulium
note: Rarest of the stable rare earths; a portable X-ray source.

name: Ytterbium
note: The atomic clock of staggering precision; a gauge that feels pressure as resistance.

name: Lutetium
note: Densest and hardest rare earth; the crystal in the PET-scan detector.

name: Hafnium
note: A neutron-drinker for reactor rods; the insulating gate inside the modern transistor.

name: Tantalum
note: Corrosion-proof; the tiny capacitor in every phone; the surgeon's implant plate.

name: Tungsten
note: Symbol W, from wolfram; the highest melting point of all metals; the bulb filament, the drill, the armor.

name: Rhenium
note: One of the rarest metals; the superalloy that lets a jet turbine take the heat.

name: Osmium
note: The densest natural element; the hard tip of the old fountain pen and the instrument pivot.

name: Iridium
note: The most corrosion-resistant metal; its thin clay layer marks the asteroid that ended the dinosaurs.

name: Platinum
note: Catalyst, jewel, and once the very definition of the kilogram; precious and unreactive.

name: Gold
note: Symbol Au, from aurum; the metal of kings, never tarnishing; alchemy's whole goal; money and microcircuits.

name: Mercury
note: Symbol Hg, from hydrargyrum; the only metal liquid at room temperature; the thermometer and the hatter's madness — quicksilver.

name: Thallium
note: 'The poisoner's poison' — tasteless, deadly; once the rat-killer and the spy's tool.

name: Lead
note: Symbol Pb, from plumbum; dense, soft, toxic; the pipe, the bullet, the radiation shield; the base metal of the Great Work.

name: Bismuth
note: Grows iridescent rainbow crystals; the pink relief of Pepto-Bismol; the last almost-stable heavy element.

name: Polonium
note: Fiercely radioactive; named for Marie Curie's Poland; an assassin's near-invisible poison.

name: Astatine
note: The rarest naturally occurring element on Earth — less than a gram exists at any moment.

name: Radon
note: A radioactive noble gas that seeps from rock into basements; a leading cause of lung cancer.

name: Francium
note: The second-rarest element; the most unstable of the first hundred-and-one; never gathered in bulk.

name: Radium
note: Curie's glowing discovery; once painted on watch dials and sold as a cure — and quietly lethal.

name: Actinium
note: First of the actinides; glows blue in the dark; a warhead aimed at cancer cells.

name: Thorium
note: A potential nuclear fuel, more abundant than uranium; the glow of the old gas-lamp mantle.

name: Protactinium
note: Rare, toxic, intensely radioactive; little beyond the research bench.

name: Uranium
note: The fuel of the reactor and the first atomic bomb; the heaviest element born in the Earth itself.

name: Neptunium
note: The first element beyond uranium; a trace in every spent fuel rod.

name: Plutonium
note: The bomb's core and the deep-space battery — it still powers the Voyagers and the Mars rovers.

name: Americium
note: The radioactive speck inside every household smoke detector.

name: Curium
note: Powers instruments on spacecraft; named for Marie and Pierre Curie.

name: Berkelium
note: A stepping-stone used to forge still-heavier elements; named for Berkeley.

name: Californium
note: A potent neutron source — it starts reactors and scans cargo for gold and oil.

name: Einsteinium
note: First found in the fallout of a hydrogen bomb; named for Einstein.

name: Fermium
note: The heaviest element reachable by reactor or explosion; named for Enrico Fermi.

name: Mendelevium
note: Named for Mendeleev, who drew the table and left gaps for the unfound.

name: Nobelium
note: Named for Alfred Nobel; made and counted a single atom at a time.

name: Lawrencium
note: The last actinide; named for Ernest Lawrence, who built the cyclotron.

name: Rutherfordium
note: The first transactinide; named for Rutherford, who split the atom's heart open.

name: Dubnium
note: Named for Dubna, the Russian laboratory that hunts the superheavy.

name: Seaborgium
note: Named for Glenn Seaborg while he still lived — a rare honor.

name: Bohrium
note: Named for Niels Bohr and his quantum atom.

name: Hassium
note: Named for Hesse, the German state of the laboratory that made it.

name: Meitnerium
note: Named for Lise Meitner, who explained nuclear fission and was passed over for the prize.

name: Darmstadtium
note: Named for Darmstadt, the city of its making; gone in moments.

name: Roentgenium
note: Named for Röntgen, who found the X-ray; exists for the blink of a nucleus.

name: Copernicium
note: Named for Copernicus; predicted to be a fleeting volatile liquid or gas.

name: Nihonium
note: The first element named in Japan ('Nihon'); a flicker of a second of existence.

name: Flerovium
note: Named for the Flerov lab; aimed at the hoped-for 'island of stability.'

name: Moscovium
note: Named for Moscow; it lives only milliseconds.

name: Livermorium
note: Named for the Livermore laboratory; among the heaviest ever assembled.

name: Tennessine
note: Named for Tennessee; a predicted halogen and the second-heaviest known element.

name: Oganesson
note: The heaviest known element; named for the living physicist Yuri Oganessian; a 'noble gas' that may be solid.
